title: Living ruled by Angels and blessed human spirits—Costerus: Saints as administrators of God’s goods
source_text: XLVIII. Praeterea statuunt Doctores Scholae Romanae, non solum ab Angelis, sed etiam a spiritibus beatorum hominum, regi & gubernari fideles viventes. Quod pluribus probare contendit Bellarminus de Sanctorum Beatitudine lib. 1. cap. 18. Similiter Costerus constare putat ex Scripturis Sanctos in caelo regnantes cum Christo haec terrena curare & administrare. Dari, scilicet, Sanctis authoritatem impios cogendi, cohibendi, puniendi, & pios ex ipsorum manibus eripiendi. Item eos esse bonorum Dei administratores. Addit Sanctos posse beneficio gloriae suae quicquid Reges potestate, quicquid opulenti divitiis, quicquid docti sapientia unquam praestare valeant. Si ergo Reges, inquit, exercitus hostiles profligant, divites egenis subveniunt, Medici arte curant; id praestare poterunt Sancti non minus, quam id praestiterunt Angeli, quorum unus 185. millia una nocte prostravit, alius Tobiae lumen reddidit, pecuniam a Gabello tulit, & nuptiis filii parentum pauperiem totamque familiam ditavit, tertius Petrum carcere liberavit, &c. In Enchiridio controversiarum cap. 12. in explicatione propositionis quartae.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover the Doctors of the Roman School maintain that the living faithful are ruled and governed not only by Angels but also by the spirits of blessed men. Which Bellarmine contends to prove with many arguments in On the Beatitude of the Saints, book 1, chapter 18. Likewise Costerus thinks it clear from the Scriptures that the Saints reigning in heaven with Christ care for and administer these earthly things. Namely that authority is given to the Saints of compelling, restraining, and punishing the impious, and of snatching the pious from their hands. Also that they are administrators of the goods of God. He adds that by the benefit of their glory the Saints can accomplish whatever Kings by power, the rich by wealth, the learned by wisdom were ever able to accomplish. If therefore Kings, he says, overthrow hostile armies, the rich aid the needy, Physicians heal by art; the Saints will be able to accomplish that no less than the Angels accomplished it, of whom one laid low 185 thousand in one night, another restored Tobias’s sight, took money from Gabelus, and by the son’s marriage enriched the parents’ poverty and whole family, a third freed Peter from prison, etc. In the Enchiridion of controversies, chapter 12, in the explanation of the fourth proposition.
pass_b_english: Roman school: Angels and blessed human spirits both rule the living.
Costerus: reigning Saints administer earthly goods—compel the impious, rescue the pious—matching angelic wonders.
